name: profile
title: Profile
description: One player's own page, in four bands: who they are, the numbers they are judged by, what they have won, and whatever else the host keeps here. The first three are an `identity`, a set of `stat`s and an `inventory`, so the avatar cases, the tabular numerals and the empty collection all behave as they do everywhere else. The profile carries no `data-gs-value` of its own: each stat answers for its own number, and a container that repeated one would leave a host asking which element it had found. An empty collection is the inventory's state and not the profile's. Loads nothing: it fetches no profile, signs nobody out and saves no setting. `player={null}` is the signed-out case and renders as one, which is what a profile tab shows before anybody signs in.
docs: Pass the adapter's `player`, or `null` before sign-in. Pass `stats` as the numbers in the order you want them, each one exactly what you would pass `stat`: the kind, the label and the format stay yours. Pass `rewards` for the collection and leave it out entirely where this player has no collection, which is not the same as an empty one; `rewards={[]}` is the empty case and `inventory` renders it. `actions` takes the controls beside the name, edit and settings, and `children` takes the rest of the page: recent results, settings rows, sign out. Those are yours because they are the application's, and this library builds no switch and submits no form. Read each number from its own stat's `data-gs-value`.
